newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia reassures China on stronger U.S. links.
newsitem.headline: Australia reassures China on stronger U.S. links.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday he would seek to ease Chinese fears over Canberra's strenthening ties with Washington in weekend talks with Chinese leader Jiang Zemin.

China had misunderstood the renewed focus on the Australia-U.S. relationship and boosted defence co-operation under the new conservative Canberra administration, Howard told reporters before leaving for Monday's summit of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Philippines.
Howard is due to meet Jiang in Manila over the weekend, but details have not been finalised.
"That will be a very important meeting," he said.
"I do think the Chinese have misunderstood the nature of the close relationship between Australia and the United States.
"That close relationship is not directed at anyone, in fact, it is a relationship that can enormously benefit the region."
Sino-Australian relations have soured during Howard's almost nine-months in office, foundering on a range of diplomatic and security issues.

The official Chinese media has expressed concern and criticised Australia over its shift towards closer ties with the United States, a traditional ally Howard says was neglected by his Asia-focussed Labor predecessors.
Leaders of the 18 Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) forum members are due to meet in Subic Bay, near Manila, on Monday for their annual summit on trade issues.
U.S. President Bill Clinton ends a five-day working holiday in Australia on Saturday, when he flies to Manila.

Australia and the United States announced boosted defence co-operation and a new security pact at top-level ministerial talks just months after Howard's coalition swept into office in a landslide election win.
